name: IL-16
label: Likely R

key_factors: R+11 district fundamentals strongly favor Republicans
LaHood holds a roughly 20-to-1 cash-on-hand advantage
Prediction markets price LaHood at about 95 percent to win
No polling indicates a competitive race
model.rationale: The forecast rests on district fundamentals: an R+11 seat, a renominated incumbent, and a lopsided financial edge for LaHood, with prediction markets and the fundamentals picture pointing the same way. Nolley's respectable fundraising is not enough evidence to move materially off that baseline.
model.watch: Any late independent polling showing Nolley within single digits, or a surge of outside spending against LaHood, would be the clearest sign the race is tightening.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
IL-16 covers north-central Illinois and leans Republican by about eleven points at the district level. Darin LaHood, the incumbent Republican, is seeking another term with a substantial financial edge, having raised roughly $4.2 million and holding $6.3 million on hand. Democrat Paul Nolley has run a credible fundraising effort for a challenger at about $600,000 raised, but trails badly in cash and has drawn essentially no outside support.

No public polls of the race are available, and prediction markets give LaHood roughly a 95 percent chance of winning. With the incumbent renominated, a dominant resource advantage, and a district that has consistently favored Republicans, the race rates as Likely Republican. Nolley would need a major shift in the national environment or unexpected evidence of weakness for LaHood to make this competitive; nothing in the current evidence points that direction.
